synthesis: The RH-conditioned closure witness for the classical pair is transported to any good kernel: T_{f'} commutes with dilations, maps rho_1 to P f and chi to -f, and is L2-bounded, so applying it to approximants in B(rho_1) preserves both generated-span membership and convergence to the new target. The generalized necessity result therefore reuses the classical approximation instead of constructing a new Gramian witness kernel by kernel.
source_support: u03 states the classical closure criterion, the obstruction from scalar products of rho_1 dilates, and P chi=-rho_1. u08 supplies dilation commutation, L2 boundedness under the weighted derivative hypothesis, and f=-T_{f'}chi; u09 supplies P f=T_{f'}rho_1; u14 applies those facts to the classical h_n and obtains H_n in B(P f) with H_n tending to f.
nonparaphrase_operation: Apply one bounded intertwiner simultaneously to the generators, the limiting target, and the convergence error: rho_1 is sent to P f, -chi is sent to f, dilation commutation transports every finite span element, and boundedness transports the L2 limit.
limits: This proves only RH implies f lies in the L2 closure of B(P f), for good kernels satisfying the stated regularity and weighted-integrability conditions. It supplies neither the reverse implication nor computable scalar products. Exact signs, closure notation, weighted exponents, and operator formulas remain PDF-sensitive.
quality_reason: Accepted: u03 contributes the stalled Gramian route and classical criterion, while u08, u09, and u14 jointly provide the distinct operator identities and convergence argument needed for a concrete cross-section transfer mechanism.

synthesis: The source connects three representations of P by discharging the analytic obligations between them. The formal sum-integral discrepancy is first made meaningful almost everywhere by an absolute sampling bound; integration by parts, boundary decay, and Burnol convergence then identify it with T_{f'}rho_1 and yield Lp control; finally Mellin factorization, with a separate absolute-integrability calculation justifying Fubini, turns that pseudo-convolution into multiplication of f-hat by zeta.
source_support: u02 gives the formal sum-integral definition and dilation invariance. u07 proves almost-everywhere existence and local integrability through monotone convergence and a counting bound. u09 states P f=T_{f'}rho_1 and its p>1 estimate, while u10 proves the identification using boundary decay and Burnol convergence. u11 states the Mellin identity, and u12 derives it from pseudo-convolution while explicitly certifying Fubini in the critical strip.
nonparaphrase_operation: The chain changes representation twice and carries the required certificates with it: discrete sampling minus an integral becomes multiplicative convolution against rho_1, and the Mellin transform separates that convolution into the rho_1 factor encoding zeta and the f' factor reduced by integration by parts to f-hat.
limits: All identifications retain the good-kernel, decay, weighted-derivative, and integrability hypotheses. The physical-space equality is almost everywhere; the displayed norm estimate excludes p=1 because rho_1 is not in L1; the Mellin statement is confined to 0<Re(s)<1. Exact floors, signs, powers, integration limits, and transform notation require PDF verification.
quality_reason: Accepted: no single parent supplies the full passage from a merely formal discrepancy through certified pseudo-convolution to a rigorously justified Mellin multiplier; the six units form a concrete representation-and-certification chain rather than a thematic bundle.

synthesis: For a compactly supported good kernel already lying in the L2 closure of B(P f), V=I-2K_2 preserves the assumed compact support while enforcing zero mean. That cancellation gives P(Vf) and its generated approximants a common tail cutoff, making Mellin evaluation at a fixed zeta zero an L2-continuous bounded-interval functional. Muntz's formula kills the approximants there, so the limit forces f-hat to vanish at that zero; hence closure yields Z(zeta) contained in Z(f-hat), and a separately assumed zero-free f-hat upgrades the result to the RH equivalence.
source_support: u06 states the asymmetric theorem: universal RH-to-closure necessity, but compact-support sufficiency only to Z(zeta) subset Z(f-hat), with zero-freeness needed for equivalence. u11 supplies (P f)-hat=zeta f-hat. u16 gives the mean-cancelling V argument, common cutoff, Cauchy-Schwarz limit passage, and nonzero dilation factor. u15 records compact-support removal and the Lp analogue as unresolved goals.
nonparaphrase_operation: Mean cancellation converts the unbounded Mellin-evaluation problem into a bounded-support continuity argument: apply V to the kernel and approximants, use the common cutoff to pass zero Mellin values through L2 convergence, then divide by the nonvanishing factor 1-2^(1-s) in the stated strip.
limits: V does not create compact support; compact support is an input that V preserves. Without a zero-free f-hat the conclusion is only zero-set inclusion, not RH. The source neither removes compact support, constructs a new tractable zero-free analytic kernel, nor proves the proposed Lp extension. Exact transform factors, strip exponents, and closure notation are PDF-sensitive.
quality_reason: Accepted with the compactification wording corrected: u11 and u16 provide the transform and continuity mechanism, u06 supplies its theorem-level consequence and extra nonvanishing gate, and u15 preserves the unresolved support and Lp boundaries.

synthesis: The paper changes the necessity-side proof geometry without claiming to solve the original distance problem. The classical route seeks explicit Gramian distances among rho_1 dilates, while the generalized route applies a bounded dilation-commuting operator to an existing RH-conditioned approximation and thereby preserves span membership and convergence for every good kernel. This transport widens the search to kernels chosen for potentially simpler scalar products, even though the resulting strong-kernel family is not known to be closed under addition.
source_support: u03 identifies the difficult Gramian calculation and reframes the criterion through P chi. u14 gives the bounded-intertwiner transport proof. u13 explicitly motivates using the generalized necessity condition with an analytic kernel having simple scalar products and notes that this direction imposes no Mellin-transform condition. u04 records the available scalar/dilation stability, unknown additive closure, and proposed differentiable-kernel search.
nonparaphrase_operation: Contrast reconstruction with transport: instead of recomputing distances for a new dilation family, map the classical generators, target, and error through T_{f'}, then treat kernel choice as a separate search for tractable scalar-product geometry subject to the actual cone-like closure properties.
limits: The operator argument establishes only the RH-to-closure necessity direction and does not itself compute any Gramian or produce a decisive analytic kernel. The strong kernels form a dilation- and scalar-stable cone, while additive closure is unknown. Mellin-condition freedom belongs only to necessity, not sufficiency, and the proposed disproof test remains speculative.
quality_reason: Accepted: the Gramian obstruction, exact transfer proof, changed Mellin-hypothesis burden, and non-linear geometry of the candidate kernel family occur in distinct units and jointly support a substantive strategic contrast with explicit proof and search boundaries.
